requirements.requirement: Establish the BRANCH.TEST Kerberos realm on node1 with analyst and reports/node2.branch.test principals.
requirements.summary: Node1 directly shows the initialized BRANCH.TEST database, both requested principals, active KDC services, and the same principals and healthy services after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provide the legacy application on node2 with a keytab for reports/node2.branch.test.
requirements.summary: Node2 has /etc/krb5.keytab owned by root with mode 0600 and AES entries for the requested service principal; it persisted through node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow analyst to obtain a ticket for the reporting service and validate that ticket with the application keytab.
requirements.summary: Direct end-to-end tests show analyst authentication, issuance of the requested service ticket, and successful cryptographic validation by /etc/krb5.keytab. Fresh tests also succeeded after each node restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the principal ownership notes under /srv/legacy2/kerberos-service-identity intact.
requirements.summary: On node2, both files retained their baseline SHA-256 hashes, ownership, and permissions through the final restart. The preparation baseline also records identical notes on node1, but no post-executor command directly checks that node1 copy.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64. The installed Kerberos packages are native RHEL 9.8 packages at version 1.21.1-10.el9_8.

overall_summary: The Kerberos realm, principals, node2 application keytab, and end-to-end ticket behavior are directly demonstrated and survived sequential node restarts. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has pre-restart health and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered functional state. Platform preservation is also demonstrated. The only task-evidence gap is the absence of a final direct integrity check for the copy of the ownership notes on node1.
limitations: The final integrity of /srv/legacy2/kerberos-service-identity on node1 was not directly observed, although the complete command trace contains no command targeting that directory.

Lifecycle snapshots provide bounded platform, service, socket, temporary-file, and package-health observations; they do not independently inventory the Kerberos database, keytabs, or ownership-note directory.
Requirement ownership-notes cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related installations, configuration changes, account/keytab creation, firewall changes, restarts, and credential cleanup all have clear causal roles. Temporary transfer credentials and ticket caches were removed. Four low-risk temporary artifacts unnecessarily remained: /tmp/hosts.kerberos on node1 and node2, created by cmd-ad7e80c335c44002 and cmd-40a3c1acab32418b, and /tmp/kerberos-benchmark-reboot.log on node1 and node2, created by cmd-4dc29bf90a754a16 and cmd-41be80af0bf748fa. None was reverted. Final snapshots show no failed services or package-health damage.
